thread:
carmen: New hire hit a weird combo on mac M1. Installed redwoodctl via brew but `redwoodctl init` created the profile then `redwoodctl serve --local` says 'no active profile'. Also login sometimes times out during device-code flow.

riley: Did brew put a shim in PATH? `which redwoodctl` and `ls -l $(which redwoodctl)`?

carmen: `which redwoodctl -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl` but it's a shim symlink to `/usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.13.2/bin/redwoodctl` that didn't match the binary I replaced earlier. I accidentally copied a manual binary to /usr/local/bin earlier and brew shim pointed elsewhere.

navin: That can create two different config locations causing profile confusion. Also Gatekeeper quarantines replaced binaries. Check `xattr -l $(which redwoodctl)` for com.apple.quarantine.
carmen: `xattr` showed quarantine on the manual binary. I removed the stray /usr/local/bin copy and reinstalled via `brew reinstall redwoodctl`. Then `redwoodctl list-profiles` shows the profile.
riley: For the device-code timeout, older clients had a short poll window and didn't surface proxy/Gatekeeper issues. Try `redwoodctl version` and if <0.13.3 upgrade. Also you can run `redwoodctl login --timeout 120s` to extend polling.
carmen: Upgraded to 0.13.4 via brew, ran `redwoodctl login --timeout 120s` and login completed. Two doc fixes: 1) quickstart should mention brew shim vs manual binary pitfalls, 2) note `--timeout` and how to check for com.apple.quarantine.
devex-bot: Opened ticket #4127: "cli: document brew shim vs manual binary pitfalls + device-code timeout guidance" assigned to @riley :spiral_note_pad:
carmen: Thanks all, saved us a support ticket.
